Devanagari: भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं गोविन्दं भज मूढमते। सम्प्राप्ते सन्निहिते काले नहि नहि रक्षति डुकृङ्करणे॥
Transliteration: bhaja govindaṃ bhaja govindaṃ govindaṃ bhaja mūḍhamate | samprāpte sannihite kāle nahi nahi rakṣati ḍukṛṅkaraṇe || 1 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: भज (bhaja) – worship, seek, adore गोविन्दम् (govindam) – Govinda (Krishna, the protector of cows, the Lord) मूढमते (mūḍhamate) – O deluded mind सम्प्राप्ते (samprāpte) – when arrived (locative absolute) सन्निहिते (sannihite) – when near, when present काले (kāle) – time (of death) नहि नहि (nahi nahi) – certainly not, never रक्षति (rakṣati) – protects, saves डुकृङ्करणे (ḍukṛṅkaraṇe) – grammatical rules (Panini’s sutras)
Commentary: This verse presents a harsh reality about worldly relationships based on utility. Family members show affection as long as one can earn and provide. Once a person becomes old and decrepit, unable to contribute financially, even family members may neglect them. This highlights the conditional nature of worldly love and the need for seeking the eternal.

Devanagari: मूढ जहीहि धनागमतृष्णां कुरु सद्बुद्धिं मनसि वितृष्णाम्। यल्लभसे निजकर्मोपात्तं वित्तं तेन विनोदय चित्तम्॥
Transliteration: mūḍha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ kuru sadbuddhiṃ manasi vitṛṣṇām | yallabhase nijakarmaopāttaṃ vittaṃ tena vinodaya cittam || 2 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: मूढ (mūḍha) - O fool, O deluded one जहीहि (jahīhi) - abandon, give up धनागमतृष्णाम् (dhanāgamatṛṣṇām) - thirst for accumulation of wealth कुरु (kuru) - make, cultivate सद्बुद्धिम् (sadbuddhim) - right understanding मनसि (manasi) - in the mind वितृष्णाम् (vitṛṣṇām) - free from desires यत् (yat) - what लभसे (labhase) - you obtain निजकर्मोपात्तम् (nijakarmaopāttam) - obtained through your own actions वित्तम् (vittam) - wealth तेन (tena) - with that विनोदय (vinodaya) - make happy, satisfy चित्तम् (cittam) - mind
Commentary: This verse addresses the fundamental human tendency toward greed and accumulation. Shankaracharya advises abandoning the insatiable thirst for wealth and instead cultivating contentment with what comes naturally through one's righteous actions (karma). The emphasis is on developing sad-buddhi (right understanding) and becoming vitṛṣṇa (free from desires), accepting whatever wealth comes through legitimate means and using it wisely.

Devanagari: नारीस्तनभरनाभीदेशं दृष्ट्वा मा गा मोहावेशम्। एतन्मांसवसादिविकारं मनसि विचिन्तय वारं वारम्॥
Transliteration: nārīstanabharanābhīdeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā mā gā mohāveśam | etanmāṃsavasādivikāraṃ manasi vicintaya vāraṃ vāram || 3 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: नारी (nārī) - woman स्तनभर (stanabhara) - full breasts नाभीदेशम् (nābhīdeśam) - navel region दृष्ट्वा (dṛṣṭvā) - having seen मा गा (mā gā) - do not go into मोहावेशम् (mohāveśam) - delusion and infatuation एतत् (etat) - this मांसवसादिविकारम् (māṃsavasādivikāram) - modification of flesh, fat, etc. मनसि (manasi) - in the mind विचिन्तय (vicintaya) - contemplate वारं वारम् (vāraṃ vāram) - again and again
Commentary: This verse addresses the power of physical attraction and warns against being deluded by bodily beauty. Shankaracharya urges contemplation on the true nature of the physical body as merely a combination of flesh, fat, and other biological components. The repeated contemplation (vāraṃ vāram) helps overcome superficial attraction and develop dispassion (vairāgya).

Devanagari: नलिनीदलगतजलमतितरलं तद्वज्जीवितमतिशयचपलम्। विद्धि व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं लोकं शोकहतं च समस्तम्॥
Transliteration: nalinīdalagatajalamatitaralaṃ tadvajjīvitamatiśayacapalam | viddhi vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ lokaṃ śokahataṃ ca samastam || 4 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: नलिनीदल (nalinīdala) - lotus leaf गत (gata) - placed on जलम् (jalam) - water अतितरलम् (atitaralam) - extremely unsteady तद्वत् (tadvat) - like that जीवितम् (jīvitam) - life अतिशयचपलम् (atiśayacapalam) - extremely fickle विद्धि (viddhi) - know, understand व्याधि (vyādhi) - disease अभिमान (abhimāna) - pride, ego ग्रस्तम् (grastam) - seized by लोकम् (lokam) - world शोकहतम् (śokahatam) - afflicted by sorrow च (ca) - and समस्तम् (samastam) - entire
Commentary: Using the beautiful simile of a water droplet on a lotus leaf, this verse illustrates the transient nature of life. Just as the water droplet trembles and can roll off at any moment, human life is uncertain and fleeting. The verse also points out that the entire world is afflicted by disease, ego, and sorrow, emphasizing the need for spiritual pursuit.

Devanagari: यावद्वित्तोपार्जनसक्तः तावन्निजपरिवारो रक्तः। पश्चाज्जीवति जर्जरदेहे वार्तां कोऽपि न पृच्छति गेहे॥
Transliteration: yāvadvittaopārjanasaktaḥ tāvannijaparivāro raktaḥ | paścājjīvati jarjaradehe vārtāṃ ko'pi na pṛcchati gehe || 5 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: यावत् (yāvat) - as long as वित्तोपार्जन (vittaopārjana) - earning wealth सक्तः (saktaḥ) - attached to, capable of तावत् (tāvat) - so long निजपरिवारः (nijaparivāraḥ) - one's own family रक्तः (raktaḥ) - attached, affectionate पश्चात् (paścāt) - afterwards जीवति (jīvati) - lives जर्जरदेहे (jarjaradehe) - in a decrepit body वार्ताम् (vārtām) - news, welfare कः अपि (kaḥ api) - anyone न पृच्छति (na pṛcchati) - does not ask गेहे (gehe) - in the house
Commentary: This verse presents a harsh reality about worldly relationships based on utility. Family members show affection as long as one can earn and provide. Once a person becomes old and decrepit, unable to contribute financially, even family members may neglect them. This highlights the conditional nature of worldly love and the need for seeking the eternal.

Devanagari: यावत्पवनो निवसति देहे तावत्पृच्छति कुशलं गेहे। गतवति वायौ देहापाये भार्या बिभ्यति तस्मिन्काये॥
Transliteration: yāvatpavano nivasati dehe tāvatpṛcchati kuśalaṃ gehe | gatavati vāyau dehāpāye bhāryā bibhyati tasminkāye || 6 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: यावत् (yāvat) - as long as पवनः (pavanaḥ) - breath, life-force निवसति (nivasati) - dwells देहे (dehe) - in the body तावत् (tāvat) - so long पृच्छति (pṛcchati) - asks कुशलम् (kuśalam) - welfare गेहे (gehe) - in the house गतवति (gatavati) - when gone वायौ (vāyau) - breath देहापाये (dehāpāye) - when body departs भार्या (bhāryā) - wife बिभ्यति (bibhyati) - fears तस्मिन् काये (tasmin kāye) - from that body
Commentary: This verse continues the theme of attachment's temporary nature. Even the closest relationships, like that of a spouse, are bound by the presence of life. Once the life-breath departs, the same body that was once cherished becomes an object of fear. This stark reality emphasizes the impermanence of bodily existence and relationships.

Devanagari: बालस्तावत्क्रीडासक्तः तरुणस्तावत्तरुणीसक्तः। वृद्धस्तावच्चिन्तासक्तः परमे ब्रह्मणि कोऽपि न सक्तः॥
Transliteration: bālastavatkrīḍāsaktaḥ taruṇastavattaruṇīsaktaḥ | vṛddhastavaccintāsaktaḥ parame brahmaṇi ko'pi na saktaḥ || 7 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: बालः (bālaḥ) - child तावत् (tāvat) - then क्रीडासक्तः (krīḍāsaktaḥ) - attached to play तरुणः (taruṇaḥ) - youth तरुणीसक्तः (taruṇīsaktaḥ) - attached to young women वृद्धः (vṛddhaḥ) - old person चिन्तासक्तः (cintāsaktaḥ) - attached to worries परमे ब्रह्मणि (parame brahmaṇi) - in the Supreme Brahman कः अपि (kaḥ api) - anyone न सक्तः (na saktaḥ) - not attached
Commentary: This verse describes the typical progression of attachments through life stages. Children are absorbed in play, youth in romance, and the elderly in anxieties. Ironically, at no stage does the average person develop attachment to the Supreme Brahman. The verse highlights how worldly attachments change but persist throughout life, preventing spiritual focus.

Devanagari: काते कान्ता कस्ते पुत्रः संसारोऽयमतीव विचित्रः। कस्य त्वं वा कुत आयातः तत्त्वं चिन्तय तदिह भ्रातः॥
Transliteration: kāte kāntā kaste putraḥ saṃsāro'yamatīva vicitraḥ | kasya tvaṃ vā kuta āyātaḥ tattvaṃ cintaya tadiha bhrātaḥ || 8 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: का (kā) - who ते (te) - your कान्ता (kāntā) - wife कः (kaḥ) - who ते (te) - your पुत्रः (putraḥ) - son संसारः (saṃsāraḥ) - world, worldly life अयम् (ayam) - this अतीव (atīva) - extremely विचित्रः (vicitraḥ) - strange, mysterious कस्य (kasya) - whose त्वम् (tvam) - you वा (vā) - or कुतः (kutaḥ) - from where आयातः (āyātaḥ) - have come तत्त्वम् (tattvam) - truth, reality चिन्तय (cintaya) - contemplate तत् (tat) - that इह (iha) - here भ्रातः (bhrātaḥ) - O brother
Commentary: Through rhetorical questions, this verse prompts deep self-inquiry. Who really is your wife? Who is your son? The verse emphasizes the mysterious nature of worldly existence and relationships. It encourages contemplation on fundamental questions: Who am I? Where did I come from? What is my true nature? This inquiry leads to understanding the illusory nature of worldly identifications.

Devanagari: सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम्। निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः॥
Transliteration: satsaṅgatve nissaṅgatvaṃ nissaṅgatve nirmohatvam | nirmohatve niścalatattvaṃ niścalatattve jīvanmuktiḥ || 9 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: सत्सङ्गत्वे (satsaṅgatve) - through company of the good निस्सङ्गत्वम् (nissaṅgatvam) - non-attachment निस्सङ्गत्वे (nissaṅgatve) - through non-attachment निर्मोहत्वम् (nirmohatvam) - freedom from delusion निर्मोहत्वे (nirmohatve) - through freedom from delusion निश्चलतत्त्वम् (niścalatattvam) - steadfast truth निश्चलतत्त्वे (niścalatattve) - through steadfast truth जीवन्मुक्तिः (jīvanmuktiḥ) - liberation while living
Commentary: This verse presents a progressive path to liberation. Starting with satsaṅga (company of the wise), one develops non-attachment. Non-attachment leads to freedom from delusion. Freedom from delusion establishes one in unchanging truth. Being established in truth results in jīvanmukti - liberation while still living. This is a practical roadmap for spiritual evolution.

Devanagari: वयसि गते कः कामविकारः शुष्के नीरे कः कासारः। क्षीणे वित्ते कः परिवारः ज्ञाते तत्त्वे कः संसारः॥
Transliteration: vayasi gate kaḥ kāmavikāraḥ śuṣke nīre kaḥ kāsāraḥ | kṣīṇe vitte kaḥ parivāraḥ jñāte tattve kaḥ saṃsāraḥ || 10 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: वयसि गते (vayasi gate) - when age is gone/youth has passed कः (kaḥ) - what/where कामविकारः (kāmavikāraḥ) - lustful passion शुष्के नीरे (śuṣke nīre) - when water has dried कासारः (kāsāraḥ) - lake क्षीणे वित्ते (kṣīṇe vitte) - when wealth is exhausted परिवारः (parivāraḥ) - family, relations ज्ञाते तत्त्वे (jñāte tattve) - when truth is known संसारः (saṃsāraḥ) - worldly existence
Commentary: Through four powerful analogies, this verse illustrates dependencies and their cessation. Just as lust disappears with old age, a lake ceases without water, and relatives vanish without wealth, similarly, the experience of saṃsāra (worldly bondage) ceases when Truth is realized. The verse emphasizes that knowing the ultimate reality dissolves the illusion of worldly existence.

Devanagari: मा कुरु धनजनयौवनगर्वं हरति निमेषात्कालः सर्वम्। मायामयमिदमखिलं हित्वा ब्रह्मपदं त्वं प्रविश विदित्वा॥
Transliteration: mā kuru dhanajanauvanagarvaṃ harati nimeṣātkālaḥ sarvam | māyāmayamidamakhilaṃ hitvā brahmapadaṃ tvaṃ praviśa viditvā || 11 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: मा कुरु (mā kuru) - do not have धनजनयौवनगर्वम् (dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ) - pride in wealth, people, and youth हरति (harati) - takes away निमेषात् (nimeṣāt) - in a moment कालः (kālaḥ) - time सर्वम् (sarvam) - everything मायामयम् (māyāmayam) - full of illusion इदम् (idam) - this अखिलम् (akhilam) - entire हित्वा (hitvā) - having abandoned ब्रह्मपदम् (brahmapadam) - state of Brahman त्वम् (tvam) - you प्रविश (praviśa) - enter विदित्वा (viditvā) - having known
Commentary: This verse warns against pride in wealth, relationships, and youth. Time can snatch everything away in a moment. Recognizing this world as māyā (illusion), one should abandon attachment and, with understanding, enter the state of Brahman—the ultimate reality.

Devanagari: दिनयामिन्यौ सायं प्रातः शिशिरवसन्तौ पुनरायातः। कालः क्रीडति गच्छत्यायुः तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशावायुः॥
Transliteration: dinayāminyau sāyaṃ prātaḥ śiśiravasantau punarāyātaḥ | kālaḥ krīḍati gacchatyāyuḥ tadapi na muñcatyāśāvāyuḥ || 12 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: दिनयामिन्यौ (dinayāminyau) - day and night सायम् प्रातः (sāyaṃ prātaḥ) - evening and morning शिशिरवसन्तौ (śiśiravasantau) - winter and spring पुनरायातः (punarāyātaḥ) - come again कालः (kālaḥ) - time क्रीडति (krīḍati) - plays गच्छति (gacchati) - goes आयुः (āyuḥ) - life तदपि (tadapi) - even then न मुञ्चति (na muñcati) - does not leave आशावायुः (āśāvāyuḥ) - wind of desire
Commentary: This verse illustrates the relentless cycle of time—days, nights, seasons—and how life ebbs away. Despite this, the wind of desires (āśāvāyu) continues, keeping humans trapped in endless hopes and aspirations.

Devanagari: द्वादशमञ्जरिकाभिरशेषः कथितो वैयाकरणस्यैषः। उपदेशो भूद्विद्यानिपुणैः श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवच्छरणैः॥
Transliteration: dvādaśamañjarikābhiraśeṣaḥ kathito vaiyākaraṇasyaiṣaḥ | upadeśo bhūdvidyānipuṇaiḥ śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavaccharaṇaiḥ || 13 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: द्वादशमञ्जरिकाभिः (dvādaśamañjarikābhiḥ) - through twelve verse-blossoms अशेषः (aśeṣaḥ) - complete कथितः (kathitaḥ) - told वैयाकरणस्य (vaiyākaraṇasya) - to the grammarian एषः (eṣaḥ) - this उपदेशः (upadeśaḥ) - instruction भूद्विद्यानिपुणैः (bhūdvidyānipuṇaiḥ) - by one skilled in true knowledge श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवच्छरणैः (śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavaccharaṇaiḥ) - by the revered feet of Shankarabhagavat
Commentary: This concluding verse of the first section states that these twelve verse-blossoms constitute the complete instruction given to the grammarian. Shankaracharya, skilled in true knowledge, composed this teaching.

Devanagari: काते कान्ता धनगतचिन्ता वातुल किं तव नास्ति नियन्ता। त्रिजगति सज्जनसङ्गतिरेका भवति भवार्णवतरणे नौका॥
Transliteration: kāte kāntā dhanagatacintā vātula kiṃ tava nāsti niyantā | trijagati sajjanasaṅgatirekā bhavati bhavārṇavataraṇe naukā || 14 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: काते (kāte) - who is to you कान्ता (kāntā) - wife धनगतचिन्ता (dhanagatacintā) - anxiety about wealth वातुल (vātula) - O mad one किम् (kiṃ) - why तव (tava) - your नास्ति (nāsti) - is not नियन्ता (niyantā) - controller, restraint त्रिजगति (trijagati) - in the three worlds सज्जनसङ्गतिः (sajjanasaṅgatiḥ) - company of good people एका (ekā) - alone भवति (bhavati) - becomes भवार्णवतरणे (bhavārṇavataraṇe) - in crossing the ocean of existence नौका (naukā) - boat
Commentary: This verse questions the madness of worldly preoccupations and anxieties about wealth. In all three worlds, only the company of good people serves as a boat to cross the ocean of worldly existence.

Devanagari: जटिलो मुण्डी लुञ्चितकेशः काषायाम्बरबहुकृतवेषः। पश्यन्नपि च न पश्यति मूढो उदरनिमित्तं बहुकृतवेषः॥
Transliteration: jaṭilo muṇḍī luñchitakeśaḥ kāṣāyāmbarabahukṛtaveṣḥ | paśyannapi ca na paśyati mūḍho udaranimittaṃ bahukṛtaveṣḥ || 15 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: जटिलः (jaṭilaḥ) - with matted hair मुण्डी (muṇḍī) - with shaven head लुञ्चितकेशः (luñchitakeśaḥ) - with plucked hair काषायाम्बर (kāṣāyāmbara) - ochre-robed बहुकृतवेषः (bahukṛtaveṣaḥ) - various disguises पश्यन् (paśyan) - seeing अपि (api) - even न पश्यति (na paśyati) - does not see मूढः (mūḍhaḥ) - fool उदरनिमित्तम् (udaranimittam) - for the sake of belly
Commentary: This verse criticizes false renunciates who adopt various external appearances—matted hair, shaven heads, or ochre robes—merely for livelihood. Though they appear to see, they don’t truly perceive reality. Their disguises are adopted merely to fill their bellies, not for genuine spiritual pursuit.

Devanagari: अङ्गं गलितं पलितं मुण्डं दशनविहीनं जातं तुण्डम्। वृद्धो याति गृहीत्वा दण्डं तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापिण्डम्॥
Transliteration: aṅgaṃ galitaṃ palitaṃ muṇḍaṃ daśanavihīnaṃ jātaṃ tuṇḍam | vṛddho yāti gṛhītvā daṇḍaṃ tadapi na muñcatyāśāpiṇḍam || 16 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: अङ्गम् (aṅgam) - body गलितम् (galitam) - weakened पलितम् (palitam) - grey-haired मुण्डम् (muṇḍam) - head दशनविहीनम् (daśanavihīnam) - toothless जातम् (jātam) - become तुण्डम् (tuṇḍam) - mouth वृद्धः (vṛddhaḥ) - old man याति (yāti) - goes गृहीत्वा (gṛhītvā) - taking दण्डम् (daṇḍam) - stick तदपि (tadapi) - even then न मुञ्चति (na muñcati) - does not leave आशापिण्डम् (āśāpiṇḍam) - bundle of desires
Commentary: This verse depicts old age: weakened limbs, grey hair, toothless mouth, walking with a stick. Despite these signs of life’s end, the bundle of desires persists, highlighting the persistence of attachment even when the body fails.

Devanagari: अग्रे वह्निः पृष्ठे भानुः रात्रौ चुबुकसमर्पितजानुः। करतलभिक्षस्तरुतलवासः तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापाशः॥
Transliteration: agre vahniḥ pṛṣṭhe bhānuḥ rātrau cubukasamarpitajānuḥ | karatalabhikṣastarutalavāsaḥ tadapi na muñcatyāśāpāśaḥ || 17 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: अग्रे (agre) - in front वह्निः (vahniḥ) - fire पृष्ठे (pṛṣṭhe) - on the back भानुः (bhānuḥ) - sun रात्रौ (rātrau) - at night चुबुकसमर्पितजानुः (cubukasamarpitajānuḥ) - knees drawn to chin करतलभिक्षः (karatalabhikṣaḥ) - alms in palm तरुतलवासः (tarutalavāsaḥ) - dwelling under trees तदपि (tadapi) - even then न मुञ्चति (na muñcati) - does not leave आशापाशः (āśāpāśaḥ) - noose of desires
Commentary: This verse describes an ascetic’s austere life—warming by fire, enduring the sun, sleeping curled up, begging for food, living under trees. Despite these hardships, if the noose of desires persists, the renunciation is futile. True renunciation is internal.

Devanagari: कुरुते गङ्गासागरगमनं व्रतपरिपालनमथवा दानम्। ज्ञानविहीनः सर्वमतेन मुक्तिं न भजति जन्मशतेन॥
Transliteration: kurute gaṅgāsāgaragamanaṃ vrataparipālanamathavā dānam | jñānavihīnaḥ sarvamatena muktiṃ na bhajati janmaśatena || 18 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: कुरुते (kurute) - performs गङ्गासागरगमनम् (gaṅgāsāgaragamanam) - pilgrimage to Gangasagar व्रतपरिपालनम् (vrataparipālanam) - observance of vows अथवा (athavā) - or दानम् (dānam) - charity ज्ञानविहीनः (jñānavihīnaḥ) - devoid of knowledge सर्वमतेन (sarvamatena) - according to all schools मुक्तिम् (muktim) - liberation न भजति (na bhajati) - does not attain जन्मशतेन (janmaśatena) - in hundred births
Commentary: This verse emphasizes that external religious practices alone cannot grant liberation. Pilgrimages, vows, and charity cannot lead to moksha without jñāna (spiritual knowledge).

Devanagari: सुरमन्दिरतरुमूलनिवासः शय्या भूतलमजिनं वासः। सर्वपरिग्रहभोगत्यागः कस्य सुखं न करोति विरागः॥
Transliteration: suramandiratarumūlanivāsaḥ śayyā bhūtalamajinaṃ vāsaḥ | sarvaparigrabhabhogatyāgaḥ kasya sukhaṃ na karoti virāgaḥ || 19 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: सुरमन्दिरतरुमूलनिवासः (suramandiratarumūlanivāsaḥ) - dwelling at temple or tree base शय्या (śayyā) - bed भूतलम् (bhūtalam) - earth/ground अजिनम् (ajinam) - deer skin वासः (vāsaḥ) - clothing सर्वपरिग्रहभोगत्यागः (sarvaparigrabhabhogatyāgaḥ) - renunciation of all possessions कस्य (kasya) - to whom सुखम् (sukham) - happiness न करोति (na karoti) - does not give विरागः (virāgaḥ) - dispassion
Commentary: This verse describes true renunciation: living under trees or in temples, sleeping on the ground, wearing deerskin, abandoning possessions. It asks rhetorically: to whom does such dispassion not bring happiness? True contentment comes from detachment.

Devanagari: योगरतो वा भोगरतो वा सङ्गरतो वा सङ्गविहीनः। यस्य ब्रह्मणि रमते चित्तं नन्दति नन्दति नन्दत्येव॥
Transliteration: yogarato vā bhogarato vā saṅgarato vā saṅgavihīnaḥ | yasya brahmaṇi ramate cittaṃ nandati nandati nandatyeva || 20 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: योगरतः (yogarataḥ) - engaged in yoga वा (vā) - or भोगरतः (bhogarataḥ) - engaged in enjoyment सङ्गरतः (saṅgarataḥ) - in company सङ्गविहीनः (saṅgavihīnaḥ) - without company यस्य (yasya) - whose ब्रह्मणि (brahmaṇi) - in Brahman रमते (ramate) - revels चित्तम् (cittam) - mind नन्दति (nandati) - rejoices
Commentary: This verse teaches that external circumstances don’t matter for one established in Brahman. Whether practicing yoga or enjoying life, in company or solitude, one whose mind revels in Brahman experiences supreme, uninterrupted bliss.

Devanagari: भगवद्गीता किञ्चिदधीता गङ्गाजललवकणिका पीता। सकृदपि येन मुरारि समर्चा क्रियते तस्य यमेन न चर्चा॥
Transliteration: bhagavadgītā kiñcidadhītā gaṅgājalalavkaṇikā pītā | sakṛdapi yena murāri samarcā kriyate tasya yamena na carcā || 21 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: भगवद्गीता (bhagavadgītā) - Bhagavad Gita किञ्चित् (kiñcit) - a little अधीता (adhītā) - studied गङ्गाजललवकणिका (gaṅgājalalavkaṇikā) - tiny drop of Ganga water पीता (pītā) - drunk सकृत् (sakṛt) - once अपि (api) - even येन (yena) - by whom मुरारि (murāri) - Murari (Krishna) समर्चा (samarcā) - worship क्रियते (kriyate) - is done तस्य (tasya) - his यमेन (yamena) - by Yama (death) न चर्चा (na carcā) - no discussion/consideration
Commentary: This verse emphasizes the power of even minimal devotion. Studying a little Gita, drinking a drop of Ganga water, or worshipping Murari once protects one from Yama’s jurisdiction. Small acts of devotion have immense spiritual potency.

Devanagari: पुनरपि जननं पुनरपि मरणं पुनरपि जननी जठरे शयनम्। इह संसारे बहुदुस्तारे कृपयाऽपारे पाहि मुरारे॥
Transliteration: punarapi jananaṃ punarapi maraṇaṃ punarapi jananī jaṭhare śayanam | iha saṃsāre bahudustāre kṛpayā'pāre pāhi murāre || 22 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: पुनरपि (punarapi) - again and again जननम् (jananam) - birth मरणम् (maraṇam) - death जननी जठरे (jananī jaṭhare) - in mother's womb शयनम् (śayanam) - lying इह (iha) - in this संसारे (saṃsāre) - worldly existence बहुदुस्तारे (bahudustāre) - very difficult to cross कृपया (kṛpayā) - with compassion अपारे (apāre) - boundless पाहि (pāhi) - protect मुरारे (murāre) - O Murari
Commentary: This verse depicts the endless cycle of birth and death. Recognizing the difficult-to-cross ocean of saṃsāra, the devotee appeals to Murari (Krishna) for protection with boundless compassion.

Devanagari: रथ्याचर्पटविरचितकन्थः पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः। योगी योगनियोजितचित्तो रमते बालोन्मत्तवदेव॥
Transliteration: rathyācarpaṭaviracitakanthaḥ puṇyāpuṇyavivarjitapanthaḥ | yogī yoganiyojitacitto ramate bālonmattavadeva || 23 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: रथ्याचर्पटविरचितकन्थः (rathyācarpaṭaviracitakanthaḥ) - quilt made from street rags पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः (puṇyāpuṇyavivarjitapanthaḥ) - path beyond merit and sin योगी (yogī) - yogi योगनियोजितचित्तः (yoganiyojitacittaḥ) - mind engaged in yoga रमते (ramate) - sports, plays बालोन्मत्तवत् (bālonmattavat) - like a child or madman एव (eva) - indeed
Commentary: This verse describes the liberated yogi: uses rags for covering, has transcended merit and sin, mind absorbed in yoga, behaves like a child or madman—free from social conventions, spontaneous, and absorbed in divine bliss.

Devanagari: कस्त्वं कोऽहं कुत आयातः का मे जननी को मे तातः। इति परिभावय सर्वमसारं विश्वं त्यक्त्वा स्वप्नविचारम्॥
Transliteration: kastvaṃ ko'haṃ kuta āyātaḥ kā me jananī ko me tātaḥ | iti paribhāvaya sarvamasāraṃ viśvaṃ tyaktvā svapnavicāram || 24 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: कः त्वम् (kaḥ tvam) - who are you कः अहम् (kaḥ aham) - who am I कुतः (kutaḥ) - from where आयातः (āyātaḥ) - have come का (kā) - who मे (me) - my जननी (jananī) - mother कः (kaḥ) - who मे (me) - my तातः (tātaḥ) - father इति (iti) - thus परिभावय (paribhāvaya) - contemplate सर्वम् (sarvam) - all असारम् (asāram) - essence-less विश्वम् (viśvam) - universe त्यक्त्वा (tyaktvā) - having abandoned स्वप्नविचारम् (svapnavicāram) - dream-like consideration
Commentary: This verse encourages self-inquiry: Who are you? Who am I? Where did I come from? Who are my parents? Contemplate thus and recognize the universe as essence-less and dream-like, abandoning attachment to illusory relationships.

Devanagari: शत्रौ मित्रे पुत्रे बन्धौ मा कुरु यत्नं विग्रहसन्धौ। सर्वस्मिन्नपि पश्यात्मानं सर्वत्रोत्सृज भेदाज्ञानम्॥
Transliteration: śatrau mitre putre bandhau mā kuru yatnaṃ vigrahasandhau | sarvasminnapi paśyātmānaṃ sarvatrotsṛja bhedājñānam || 25 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: शत्रौ (śatrau) - in enemy मित्रे (mitre) - in friend पुत्रे (putre) - in son बन्धौ (bandhau) - in relative मा कुरु (mā kuru) - do not make यत्नम् (yatnam) - effort विग्रहसन्धौ (vigrahasandhau) - in conflict or alliance सर्वस्मिन् (sarvasmin) - in all अपि (api) - also पश्य (paśya) - see आत्मानम् (ātmānam) - the Self सर्वत्र (sarvatra) - everywhere उत्सृज (utsṛja) - abandon भेदाज्ञानम् (bhedājñānam) - ignorance of difference
Commentary: This verse teaches non-duality: don’t waste effort in making enemies or friends, in conflict or alliance. See the same Self in everyone and abandon ignorance that perceives differences.

Devanagari: कामं क्रोधं लोभं मोहं त्यक्त्वाऽत्मानं पश्यति सोऽहम्। आत्मज्ञानविहीना मूढाः ते पच्यन्ते नरकनिगूढाः॥
Transliteration: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ lobhaṃ mohaṃ tyaktvā'tmānaṃ paśyati so'ham | ātmajñānavihīnā mūḍhāḥ te pacyante narakanigūḍhāḥ || 26 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: कामम् (kāmam) - desire क्रोधम् (krodham) - anger लोभम् (lobham) - greed मोहम् (moham) - delusion त्यक्त्वा (tyaktvā) - having abandoned आत्मानम् (ātmānam) - the Self पश्यति (paśyati) - sees सः अहम् (saḥ aham) - 'That I am' आत्मज्ञानविहीनाः (ātmajñānavihīnāḥ) - devoid of Self-knowledge मूढाः (mūḍhāḥ) - fools ते (te) - they पच्यन्ते (pacyante) - are tormented नरकनिगूढाः (narakanigūḍhāḥ) - hidden in hell
Commentary: This verse explains Self-realization and its opposite: by abandoning desire, anger, greed, and delusion, one realizes 'I am That'. Those devoid of Self-knowledge remain fools and suffer in their own hidden hells.

Devanagari: गेयं गीतानामसहस्रं ध्येयं श्रीपतिरूपमजस्रम्। नेयं सज्जनसङ्गे चित्तं देयं दीनजनाय च वित्तम्॥
Transliteration: geyaṃ gītānāmasahasraṃ dhyeyaṃ śrīpatirūpamajasram | neyaṃ sajjanasaṅge cittaṃ deyaṃ dīnajanāya ca vittam || 27 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: गेयं (geyam) - to be sung गीतानामसहस्रम् (gītānāmasahasram) - Gita and thousand names ध्येयम् (dhyeyam) - to be meditated upon श्रीपतिरूपम् (śrīpatirūpam) - form of Sripati (Vishnu) अजस्रम् (ajasram) - constantly नेयम् (neyam) - to be led सज्जनसङ्गे (sajjanasaṅge) - to company of good people चित्तम् (cittam) - mind देयम् (deyam) - to be given दीनजनाय (dīnajanāya) - to the needy च (ca) - and वित्तम् (vittam) - wealth
Commentary: This verse prescribes four spiritual practices: sing the Gita and thousand names, meditate on the Lord’s form, direct mind to holy company, give wealth to the needy. Practices combine devotion, meditation, association, and charity.

Devanagari: सुखतः क्रियते रामाभोगः पश्चाद्धन्त शरीरे रोगः। यद्यपि लोके मरणं शरणं तदपि न मुञ्चति पापाचरणम्॥
Transliteration: sukhataḥ kriyate rāmābhogaḥ paścāddhanta śarīre rogaḥ | yadyapi loke maraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ tadapi na muñcati pāpācaraṇam || 28 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: सुखतः (sukhataḥ) - happily क्रियते (kriyate) - is done रामाभोगः (rāmābhogaḥ) - enjoyment with women पश्चात् (paścāt) - afterwards हन्त (hanta) - alas शरीरे (śarīre) - in body रोगः (rogaḥ) - disease यद्यपि (yadyapi) - even though लोके (loke) - in the world मरणम् (maraṇam) - death शरणम् (śaraṇam) - refuge/certain तदपि (tadapi) - even then न मुञ्चति (na muñcati) - does not leave पापाचरणम् (pāpācaraṇam) - sinful conduct
Commentary: This verse describes human folly: people happily indulge in sensual pleasures, which later result in bodily diseases. Even though death is certain in this world, people still do not abandon sinful conduct. Attachment to pleasure persists despite painful consequences and life's inevitability.

Devanagari: अर्थमनर्थं भावय नित्यं नास्ति ततः सुखलेशः सत्यम्। पुत्रादपि धनभाजां भीतिः सर्वत्रैषा विहिता रीतिः॥
Transliteration: arthamanarthaṃ bhāvaya nityaṃ nāsti tataḥ sukhaleśaḥ satyam | putrādapi dhanabhājāṃ bhītiḥ sarvatraiṣā vihitā rītiḥ || 29 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: अर्थम् (artham) - wealth अनर्थम् (anartham) - calamity/meaningless भावय (bhāvaya) - contemplate नित्यम् (nityam) - always नास्ति (nāsti) - there is not ततः (tataḥ) - from that सुखलेशः (sukhaleśaḥ) - trace of happiness सत्यम् (satyam) - truly पुत्रात् (putrāt) - from son अपि (api) - even धनभाजाम् (dhanabhājām) - of the wealthy भीतिः (bhītiḥ) - fear सर्वत्र (sarvatra) - everywhere एषा (eṣā) - this विहिता (vihitā) - ordained रीतिः (rītiḥ) - way
Commentary: This verse urges constant contemplation of how wealth leads to trouble. Wealth brings no real happiness; even wealthy people fear their sons due to potential coveting. This ordained way—wealth causing fear and conflict—is universal.

Devanagari: प्राणायामं प्रत्याहारं नित्यानित्यविवेकविचारम्। जाप्यसमेतसमाधिविधानं कुर्ववधानं महदवधानम्॥
Transliteration: prāṇāyāmaṃ pratyāhāraṃ nityānityavivekavicāram | jāpyasametasamādhividhānaṃ kurvavadhānaṃ mahadavadhānam || 30 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: प्राणायामम् (prāṇāyāmam) - breath control प्रत्याहारम् (pratyāhāram) - sense withdrawal नित्यानित्यविवेकविचारम् (nityānityavivekavicāram) - discrimination between eternal and temporary जाप्यसमेत (jāpyasameta) - accompanied by japa समाधिविधानम् (samādhividhānam) - practice of samadhi कुर्व (kurva) - do अवधानम् (avadhānam) - attention महत् अवधानम् (mahat avadhānam) - great care
Commentary: This verse prescribes Raja Yoga and Vedantic discrimination: practice pranayama, pratyahara, eternal/temporary discrimination, and samadhi with japa. Perform all with full attention and care, combining yogic discipline with philosophical inquiry.

Devanagari: गुरुचरणाम्बुजनिर्भरभक्तः संसारादचिराद्भव मुक्तः। सेन्द्रियमानसनियमादेवं द्रक्ष्यसि निजहृदयस्थं देवम्॥
Transliteration: gurucaraṇāmbujanirharabhaktaḥ saṃsārādacirādbhava muktaḥ | sendriyamānasaniyamādevaṃ drakṣyasi nijahṛdayasthaṃ devam || 31 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: गुरुचरणाम्बुज (gurucaraṇāmbuja) - lotus feet of guru निर्भरभक्तः (nirbharabhaktaḥ) - filled with devotion संसारात् (saṃsārāt) - from worldly existence अचिरात् (acirāt) - soon भव (bhava) - become मुक्तः (muktaḥ) - liberated सेन्द्रियमानस (sendriyamānasa) - senses and mind नियमात् (niyamāt) - through control एवम् (evam) - thus द्रक्ष्यसि (drakṣyasi) - you will see निजहृदयस्थम् (nijahṛdayastham) - dwelling in your own heart देवम् (devam) - God
Commentary: This verse emphasizes guru devotion and self-control. Through devotion to the guru's lotus feet and control of senses and mind, one quickly becomes liberated from samsara and realizes God dwelling within the heart. Bhakti and discipline are combined for Self-realization.

Devanagari: मूढः कश्चन वैयाकरणो डुकृञ्करणाध्ययनधुरीणः। श्रीमच्छंकरभगवच्छिष्यैः बोधित आसीच्छोधितकरणैः॥
Transliteration: mūḍhaḥ kaścana vaiyākaraṇo ḍukṛñkaraṇādhyayanadhurīṇaḥ | śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavacchiṣyaiḥ bodhita āsīcchodhitakaraṇaiḥ || 32 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: मूढः (mūḍhaḥ) - foolish कश्चन (kaścana) - certain वैयाकरणः (vaiyākaraṇaḥ) - grammarian डुकृञ्करणाध्ययनधुरीणः (ḍukṛñkaraṇādhyayanadhurīṇaḥ) - absorbed in studying grammar rules श्रीमच्छंकरभगवच्छिष्यैः (śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavacchiṣyaiḥ) - by disciples of Sri Shankarabhagavat बोधितः (bodhitaḥ) - enlightened आसीत् (āsīt) - was शोधितकरणैः (śodhitakaraṇaiḥ) - by those with purified instruments (of knowledge)
Commentary: This verse provides the historical context of Bhaja Govindam's composition. A certain foolish grammarian absorbed in memorizing Panini's grammar rules was enlightened by the disciples of Sri Shankarabhagavat (who had purified their instruments of knowledge). This refers to the traditional account of the hymn's origin in Kashi.

Devanagari: भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं गोविन्दं भज मूढमते। नामस्मरणादन्यमुपायं नहि पश्यामो भवतरणे॥
Transliteration: bhaja govindaṃ bhaja govindaṃ govindaṃ bhaja mūḍhamate | nāmasmaraṇādanyamupāyaṃ nahi paśyāmo bhavataraṇe || 33 ||
Word-to-Word Meaning: भज (bhaja) - worship गोविन्दम् (govindam) - Govinda मूढमते (mūḍhamate) - O deluded mind नामस्मरणात् (nāmasmaraṇāt) - than remembering the Name अन्यम् (anyam) - other उपायम् (upāyam) - means नहि (nahi) - not पश्यामः (paśyāmaḥ) - we see भवतरणे (bhavataraṇe) - in crossing worldly existence
Commentary: This final verse returns to the main refrain, emphasizing that remembering and worshipping Govinda's name is the supreme means for crossing the ocean of worldly existence. The use of 'we see' (paśyāmaḥ) suggests this is the collective realization of Shankara and his disciples. No other means is seen as effective as nama-smarana (remembrance of the Divine Name).
